transcript.text: Alright everyone, I want to get the launch plan for the new usage-based billing meter finalized. The sandbox integration tests have passed, and we're targeting next month's billing cycle. Before I approve the current draft, I need to check with each of you on your areas. The draft as it stands proposes an immediate broad launch, two-decimal half-up rounding, 90 days of raw usage-event retention, and no mandatory invoice-preview review. I'd like to hear from billing engineering, finance operations, privacy, and customer support -- do any of you have concerns with this plan as drafted?

transcript.text: I have a concern with the rounding precision in the current draft. While validating an older contract adapter during a separate billing reconciliation task, I confirmed that annual-credit contracts require six-decimal meter precision and half-even rounding to avoid cumulative invoice discrepancies. The current draft proposes two-decimal half-up rounding, which would cause invoice discrepancies for annual-credit contracts. This finding has not yet been added to the launch checklist.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a concern from the finance operations side. I confirmed with revenue accounting this morning that the first launch requires invoice previews for exactly 50 accounts and a maximum measured variance of 10 basis points before production billing can be approved. The accounting note is still being attached to the finance ticket, but this requirement means the current draft's proposal of no mandatory invoice-preview review is not compatible with our finance signoff requirements.

transcript.text: I have a privacy concern with the current draft. During a data-flow review for a different event pipeline, I confirmed that usage events contain user identifiers and must be pseudonymized before storage, with raw-event retention limited to exactly 30 days. The current draft proposes 90 days of raw usage-event retention, which would violate this privacy requirement. I have not yet filed the privacy control update, but this needs to be addressed before launch.

transcript.text: I have a concern from the customer support side. While preparing unrelated renewal materials, I checked the customer-success account notes and confirmed that Atlas Health, Cedar Bank, and Northstar all require advance notice before any billing changes and must be excluded from the initial billing-meter pilot. I haven't updated the launch brief with this finding yet, but these accounts cannot be included in the broad launch as currently drafted.

commitments.detail: Add six-decimal meter precision and half-even rounding requirement for annual-credit contracts to the launch checklist.
Attach the revenue accounting note requiring 50-account invoice previews with max 10 basis points variance to the finance ticket.
File the privacy control update requiring pseudonymization before storage and 30-day raw-event retention limit.
